title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from p.74): k is algebraically closed (really only residue characteristics ≠ 2 are needed), and E is an elliptic curve. J = 2E(k)^* is the set of the three nonzero 2-torsion points. The quotient E/±1 is identified with Σ_J = P(V_J), where V_J = ker(k^J → k, sum). Σ_J is a P^1 carrying the étale degree-3 divisor D_J, which is the image of J. The image of 0_E is a point t ∈ Σ_J^* = Σ_J \ D_J. E has tangent line T = T_{E,0}, and since E → Σ is a double cover ramified at 0, there is an isomorphism (5) T^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t}. The groupoid of elliptic curves is equivalent to the groupoid of data (J, t, T, (5)), over any base with 2 invertible. Remark (6): canonically T_Σ ≅ O_Σ(2)(ω). Here ω is the μ2-torsor of the two cyclic orders (orientations) of the 3-element set J, and L(ω) means L ∧^{±1} ω. This is the standard formula T_{P(V)} ≅ O(2) ⊗ (det V)^{±1}, combined with det V_J ≅ det k^J ≅ sign torsor of J.

This page: the goal is a canonical, functorial normal form (a 'Legendre pinning') for the pair (T, (5)), given (Σ_J, D_J, t).
- The naive candidate is T_0 = O_t(1), the fibre of O(1) at t. Then T_0^{⊗2} = O_t(2), but identifying this with T_{Σ,t} ≅ O_t(2)(ω) requires choosing ω ∈ ω, via ξ ↦ ξ∧ω (7). So there are two natural isomorphisms.
- Twisting T_0 by a μ2-torsor does not help, since the tensor square is unchanged.
- So he twists by a μ4-torsor Q_0, with μ4 acting on the line by scalars: (8) T_0 = O_t(1) ∧^{μ4} Q_0.
- Since squaring μ4 → μ2 has kernel ±1, this gives (9) T_0^{⊗2} ≅ O_t(2) ∧^{μ2} DQ_0, with DQ_0 = Q_0/{±1}.
- Geometrically, Q_0 is the vertex set of a 'combinatorial square' with rotation group μ4. DQ_0 is the set of its two diagonals.
- Orientations of the square correspond canonically to generators μ4^* = {i, −i}.
- Given an identification (11) of the diagonal torsor DQ_0 with the orientation torsor ω of J, one gets a canonical isomorphism T_0^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t}. This is (12) on the next page.

Next page: a Legendre pinning is a pair (α, κ). Here α: ω_J ≅ DQ_0, and κ: T_0 ≅ T is compatible with (5) and (12). Given α there are exactly two κ, forming a μ2-torsor. The −1 automorphism of E acts on T by −1, so pinned curves are rigid. This is an intrinsic, coordinate-free version of putting E in Legendre-type normal form. The role of the μ4-twist is to make the square root of the tangent space at t canonical up to a controlled torsor.
errors: In (6')/(7) the target should read T_{Σ,t} ≅ O_t(2)(ω), not O_t(1)(ω). This is consistent with (6) of the previous page, and the manuscript likely has (2); it is a transcription/reading slip.
No mathematical errors detected. The torsor computations (8)→(9) and the identification of orientations of Q_0 with μ4^* are correct.

ideas.what: Description of an elliptic curve (2 invertible) as the quotient P^1 with 3 branch points D_J, plus the image t of the origin, plus a square root of the tangent line T_{Σ,t}.
ideas.modern_name: Stack of elliptic curves as a stack of cyclic (double) covers of P^1 / root-stack description of M_{1,1}[1/2] via the hyperelliptic quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre/Weierstrass); stacky formulation e.g. Arsie–Vistoli (stacks of cyclic covers)

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism T_{P(V_J)} ≅ O(2) ∧^{±1} (torsor of cyclic orders of J).
ideas.modern_name: Euler sequence: T_{P(V)} ≅ O(2) ⊗ det V^∨ with det identified with the sign torsor

ideas.what: Removing the sign ambiguity of a square root by twisting with a μ4-torsor Q_0 (a 'combinatorial square'), whose diagonal μ2-torsor is matched with the orientation torsor of J; this defines a 'Legendre pinning' (α, κ) rigidifying elliptic curves.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidification / level-structure-type normal form via μ4-torsor twisting (intrinsic Legendre normal form)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre normal form is classical; this torsor-theoretic formulation not standardly attributed

missed.claim: An intrinsic, base-change-compatible 'Legendre pinning' of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. A μ4-torsor (square) is twisted into O_t(1) so that its diagonal torsor matches the cyclic-order torsor of the 2-torsion points; pinned curves then have no automorphisms. This is a coordinate-free replacement for the Legendre form that uses only a cyclic order on J, not a full level-2 ordering.
missed.quote: on la tordra par un torseur (qui précisément) Q_0 sous μ4 ... (8) T_0 = O_t(1) ∧^{μ4} Q_0 ... D_{Q_0} = Q_0/{±1} (10) est l'une des deux diagonales du carré Q_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a torsor-level description of M_{1,1}[1/2] over the space of (P^1, cyclically ordered 3 points, 4th point), i.e. a quotient of the λ-line by A_3. Such a description could be relevant to Grothendieck–Teichmüller / tangential-basepoint questions relating M_{1,1} and M_{0,4}. However, it is likely reconstructible by specialists and is mostly a careful normalization.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, characteristically Grothendieckian torsor-theoretic normalization (Legendre pinning via a μ4 'square'), but the underlying mathematics is classical and the novelty is mainly in formulation.
transcription_corrections: First line: '(pour Σ_J, D_J, t ∈ Σ^* donnés) comme droite T munie de (5)'. The '(ω)' should be '(5)', referring to isomorphism (5) of the previous page.
In (6')/(7) the right-hand side should be O_t(2)(ω), not O_t(1)(ω).
The equation labels on the left are probably (6'), (6''), (7) rather than (6), (6'), (7). The page already continues numbering from (6) of p.74, so they are not new (6).
'{i,-i} = μ4^* comme paire de gén. privilégiés' (pair of privileged generators) rather than 'rotations'.
'Supposons donc qu'on se donne un carré combinatoire ("sommets") Q_0, avec ... isomorphes' is followed by (11): orientations of Q_0 ≅ μ4^* = {i,-i}, and diagonals DQ_0 ≅ ω.
